chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Isa ibn Suleyman al-Nahhas, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Khaybari and Yunus ibn Zabyan, both of whom said:
We heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: There is nothing more beloved to Allah than bringing out dirhams to the Imam, and Allah shall indeed make for him, in Paradise, the dirham like Mount Uhud.
Then he said: Allah, the Exalted, says in His Book:
Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him many times over?
He said: By Allah, it is specifically regarding maintaining support of the Imam.

key_terms.إِخْرَاجِ: bringing forth or spending out wealth
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: silver coins or money given financially
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the place of eternal reward
key_terms.قَرْضًا حَسَنًا: a goodly loan, meaning sincere spending for Allah
key_terms.يُقْرِضُ: lends, used for giving in Allah's cause

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the meaning of lending Allah a goodly loan in relation to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that spending one's wealth for the Imam is among the most beloved acts to Allah and carries immense reward in Paradise. It then applies the Qur'anic expression of a 'goodly loan' to Allah specifically to supporting the Imam, presenting such financial support as a divinely multiplied act of devotion and loyalty.
